Developer Certificate of Origin 1.1: by signing off, a contributor certifies (a) they wrote it and may submit it under the file's open source licence, (b) it is based on compatibly licensed work, or (c) it was passed to them by someone who certified (a)-(c), and (d) the contribution record is public and kept indefinitely; it grants no extra licence.

Home Assistant's 'Contributor License Agreement' is the Linux DCO modified to name Apache 2.0 and drop sign-off; it was adopted 2017-01-28 and a signing link is generated automatically on a contributor's first pull request. It is not a copyright assignment.
GitLab replaced its Contributor License Agreement with the DCO on 2017-11-01, saying the CLA was a deterrent to contributing for some of its community.
